predecessors.name: Buyid dynasty
predecessors.text: lands between Kufa and Hit, granted by the Buyid emir Mu'izz al-Dawla between 956 and 963 "in return for military service"

successors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
successors.text: Hilla, occupied by Abbasid forces in 1163: "Mazyadid rule came to an end"

ledger.x: c. 961: the Buyids settle the Banu Asad between Kufa and Hit. 'Between 956 and 963, the Buyid emir Mu'izz al-Dawla granted the Mazyadids titles, subsidies, and lands between Kufa and Hit in return for military service'.
1163: the Mazyadid emirate ends with the Abbasid occupation of Hilla.

wars.name: Seljuk war against Sadaqa I
wars.outcome: Sadaqa I, at the height of his power under the weak Barkiyaruq (1092-1105), was "defeated and killed in battle in 1108" by the Seljuk sultan's army; Dubays II succeeded and Hilla stayed Mazyadid.

wars.name: Mazyadid-Zengi war against the Abbasid caliph and Seljuks
wars.outcome: Zengi defeated Dubays II at the Battle of Mubarraqiyya (March 1123); on 20 June 1132 Dubays and Zengi were defeated by the caliph al-Mustarshid at Hisn al-Baramika, north of Baghdad.

certainty.note: A tribal emirate with a core at Kufa, Hit and Hilla; the pages give no frontiers and no area.
